dedupe_keys.name: mount polley tailings storage facility breach independent expert investigation 2014 2015

description: On 4 August 2014 the tailings storage facility of the Mount Polley copper and gold mine in British Columbia, Canada, breached and released tailings and water into Polley Lake, Hazeltine Creek and Quesnel Lake. On 18 August 2014 an independent panel of three geotechnical experts was set up to investigate the causes, and on 30 January 2015 it delivered its final report and recommendations to the British Columbia Minister of Energy and Mines and to the Williams Lake and Soda Creek Indian Bands. The website publishes the full report and all appendices free of charge: terms of reference, surface and subsurface investigations with borehole, cone penetration, vane shear and pressuremeter test data, laboratory testing, instrumentation records, the water balance, breach analysis and a 3D flyover. The report concluded that the failure was an undrained failure in a glaciolacustrine layer (the Upper GLU) of the dam foundation, and made recommendations for tailings dam practice. No licence is stated for the documents. Caveats: it is a single-site post-event study whose data were collected for the investigation. For simulation it is a validated post-event case for dam-breach, geotechnical fragility and downstream cascading-impact models of tailings facilities. Related catalogue records include the Global Tailings Portal and the WISE Uranium chronology of tailings dam failures.
